Title: error when Zipping 2 publish subjects asynchroneously
Description: Hi,

I'm having some weird problem I've tried to simplify.

Take for instance the following code:

``` java
        for (int i = 0; i < 500; i++) {
            Subject<Integer, Integer> s1 = PublishSubject.<Integer> create().toSerialized();
            Subject<Integer, Integer> s2 = PublishSubject.<Integer> create().toSerialized();

            Observable.zip(s1.single(), s2.toList(), (a, b) -> null)
                .subscribeOn(Schedulers.io())
                .subscribe(
                    j -> {},
                    t -> {
                        t.printStackTrace();
                    });

            s1.onNext(1);
            s2.onNext(1);
            s1.onCompleted();
            s2.onCompleted();
        }
        Thread.sleep(5000);
```

REASONING: This issue is about a race condition in RxJava where using `subscribeOn(Schedulers.io())` causes problems with the ordering of events in PublishSubjects. The user has already identified that removing the `subscribeOn` call fixes the issue, but wants to understand why. 

This is a conceptual threading/concurrency issue that can be verified through code analysis without needing to build and run the code. The problem occurs because `subscribeOn` moves subscription to a different thread, which can cause race conditions with the immediate emission of events right after subscription.

An expert can analyze the code and explain that when using `subscribeOn`, the subscription happens asynchronously on the IO thread, but the code continues executing on the main thread and immediately calls `onNext` and `onCompleted`. This creates a race condition where sometimes the events are processed before the subscription is fully established.

The solution (removing `subscribeOn` or ensuring proper synchronization) can be validated through understanding of RxJava's concurrency model without needing to reproduce the exact error. This is a classic concurrency pattern issue that can be analyzed conceptually.
